messages:
devin: Quick proposal — adjust prefetch budget per-device based on KV-page fragmentation + seqlen distribution. I sketched some heuristics and a small perf run. cc @maria @cheng

maria: LGTM to exploring. can you paste the heuristics? curious how this interacts with our MQA path selection.

devin: Here are the heuristics I used in the probe (very rough):
```
// per-device budget B = min(max_prefetch, base + alpha * hot_fragmentation + beta * seqlen_tail_ratio)
// hot_fragmentation = fraction of KV pages with >X live segments
// seqlen_tail_ratio = pct requests > 512 tokens / pct requests > 128 tokens
// base tuned by GPU mem bandwidth profile
```

devin: Rationale: paged-KV prefetch helps GQA when hot pages cross batch boundaries. But on MQA with many short sequences prefetch noise kills L2 throughput. So budget should shrink when seqlen_tail_ratio is low.

cheng: Nice. any numbers from the probe?

devin: Small run on p4d-like nodes, 4k requests synthetic across mixed seqlens. Key metrics (median token/sec):
- baseline (fixed B=64): 1200 tok/s
- adaptive B (heuristic above): 1375 tok/s (+14.6%)
- aggressive B=128: 1320 tok/s (+10%) but 95th latency regressed by ~18%

sam: Did you try toggling for MQA vs GQA workloads separately?

devin: Yeah:
- pure GQA (longer tails): adaptive B -> +22% throughput, no tail latency hit.
- pure MQA (many <64 seqs): adaptive B -> slight throughput +2%, but aggressive B regressed 95th a lot.

maria: That suggests the autotuner should bias toward smaller budgets when MQA probability is high. How to detect MQA vs GQA online w/o heavy sampling?

devin: Use a lightweight seqlen histogram per-route (exponential decay window). If >X% of requests <64 tokens -> mark MQA-dominant. Also watch KV hit-ratio spike pattern (MQA tends to have very shallow KV reuse).

cheng: What about kernel pick interplay? If we lower prefetch budget but keep using wide-block paged-attn kernels, could we lose benefits?

devin: Good point. In the probe we coupled budget with kernel selector: when prefetch budget < threshold, force narrow-block paged-attn path (lower memory footprint kernels). That avoided regressions.

jen: ops-bot kicked off the longer perf job a minute ago: perf-run-3417773332-adaptive-200k. I'll post logs when done. :eyes:

ops-bot: perf-run-3417773332-adaptive-200k started on cluster-phi. job id 0x8f4. ETA ~25m.

sam: For rollout, suggest canary that flips selector + prefetch tuning for single model family first (llamaX-13B) in europe region. Keep a rollback flag.

maria: Also add trace points for: per-request chosen budget, kernel path, KV pages prefetched, and whether hit came from hot cache. That helped debug earlier weirdness.

devin: Agreed — I'll add those traces and the histogram metric. Also will expose the tuner outputs to the Console as a per-route suggestion so SEs can opt-in.

cheng: One more ask: quantify GPU L2 traffic and SM occupancy for each setting. the perf numbers without hw counters are noisy.

devin: Got it. next run will capture nvprof counters (L2_loads, dram_bw, sm_efficiency).

jen: perf-run finished. summary (quick): adaptive B gives +13% median throughput, 95th improved by 5% for mixed workload. Logs uploaded to s3://redwood-perf/3417773332/summary.log

maria: Nice. can you open a short PR with tuner impl + config flags? I'll review and we can schedule a canary.

devin: Will do. PR will include tests that assert no 95th latency regression on MQA synthetic profile.

sam: FYI: watch out for interaction with cache-eviction hysteresis. last time we saw oscillation when tuner adjusted budget too fast. Add a min dwell time.

devin: Good catch. adding 3-min dwell and step limited changes (max 20% change per minute).

cheng: Thanks — this looks like a solid path. if canary is green, next target is adding architecture-aware default params (ampere vs hopper).

maria: :thumbsup: keep the notes in GH issue #runtime-prefetch so we don't lose them.

devin: Done, linked the perf runs and heuristics in the issue. closing thread for now unless ops-bot finds a regression.

ops-bot: No regressions detected in canary window so far (10m).
